name: Autism
summary: Autism is a lifelong and heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition or identity associated with differences in social communication, patterns of behaviour or interests, and sensory experience, with widely varying strengths and support needs.

includes: support, access, and environmental fit across the lifespan
excludes: a single presentation or support profile
claims that one language preference fits every autistic person

claims.text: Autistic people's abilities and support needs vary substantially and may change across contexts and over time.
Sensory hyperreactivity, hyporeactivity, or unusual sensory interests can be part of autistic experience, but sensory profiles are heterogeneous.

sources.citation: World Health Organization. Autism fact sheet (17 September 2025).
Kawakami, S. et al. Neurobiology of sensory processing in autism spectrum disorder (2020).

uncertainties.question: How can research and services represent changing, context-dependent support needs without collapsing people into functioning labels?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: Poor categories can hide support needs, autonomy, or strengths.
what_would_reduce_it: validation across ages, cultures, communication modes, and intellectual abilities

uncertainties.question: Which sensory measures predict useful, person-defined accommodations across settings?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: Group findings do not identify what will help a particular person.
what_would_reduce_it: reporting of benefit, burden, and adverse effects

perspectives.summary: Autism is a diverse group of conditions related to brain development, with variable abilities and needs requiring accessible and inclusive support.

relations.note: Autism is commonly situated within neurodiversity discourse.
Sensory differences are common but heterogeneous.
Executive demands can shape daily access and support; this is not a defining equivalence.

questions: Does the autistic person control and evaluate the accommodation?
Are communication access and safeguarding explicit?
What outcome and context support the claim?
Can the tool increase distress, surveillance, or dependency?
Are non-speaking people and people with high support needs represented?

provenance.method: Structured synthesis of cited public sources; no community review yet
